items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I saw John Lindsay he was a trombone player but he couldn‟t compete with Kid Oray and with Preston Jackson.

ctx.x: Yeah. Now the trombone players, they don‟t need all the tailgaters on the back of the trucks no more. They don‟t need all these tailgaters in Chicago so only the good trombone players survived, Kid Oray, Preston Jackson, they survived. There were a lot of trombone players like Jimmy Newman, who would probably have a clarinet and one trombone and the next place would have maybe a trombone and a trumpet so there weren‟t three or four trombones. So trombone players were beginning to get scarce. So later you see why…
And he was playing bass lines anyway.
